message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower from scratch would be a massive undertaking—think of a 324‑meter‑tall lattice structure with thousands of steel panels, rivets, and exposed surfaces. Even though the tower is routinely repainted every 7–10 years (the current paint job started in 2019 and is scheduled to finish in 2026), a fresh, full‑coverage paint job would involve:

| Task | Rough Time |
|------|------------|
| **Surface prep** (cleaning, rust removal, priming) | 2–3 months |
| **Primer application** | 1–2 months |
| **Top‑coat layers** (multiple coats, drying time between each) | 3–4 months |
| **Detail work** (corners, railings, decorative elements) | 1–2 months |
| **Inspection & touch‑ups** | 1 month |

Adding up the phases, a full repaint could take **roughly 9–12 months** if you have a dedicated crew working continuously. In practice, the actual schedule would be spread over several years because the tower is open to the public and must remain operational, so crews work in shifts and often during off‑peak hours.

So, if you’re planning a one‑off repaint, expect a year or more of work—though the tower’s regular maintenance schedule keeps it looking fresh without a single, continuous paint‑job.
